summary: Milestone execution completed 10 experiments in 275.1 minutes; 2 were compute-bound. In the bounded slowest list, the compute-bound entries took 33.3 and 18.72 minutes, but causal phase timing was unavailable. The locked task-conditioned idle indicator is false, and no concurrent multi-model task is identified, so neither utilization inefficiency nor a DualGPURunner miss is established.
bottlenecks_identified: The synthesis-only reconciliation task was the largest recorded slow path at 114.9 minutes, making reconciliation throughput the clearest operational bottleneck.
The synthesis-only Rust parity port was the next-longest task at 42.63 minutes, but the supplied data has no phase breakdown showing where that time accumulated.
The compute-bound entries took 33.3 and 18.72 minutes; the supplied data identifies their workloads but does not provide causal phase telemetry for either duration.
improvements_suggested: Create a schema-validated reconciliation scaffold that is updated throughout the milestone to reduce end-loaded closeout assembly.
Add phase-level timers and dependency-wait receipts to every experiment, with explicit stages for reconciliation and parity workflows.
Record task-scoped GPU utilization, declared model concurrency, and runner selection for every compute-bound task; select DualGPURunner only for concurrent multi-model work.
Dispatch dependency-independent synthesis work concurrently when the milestone graph permits it.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Continuously assemble and schema-check reconciliation evidence before closeout.
Emit phase-level timing and dependency-wait receipts for every experiment.
Capture task-scoped GPU, model-concurrency, and runner-selection telemetry for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The savings estimate is conditional: halving the 114.9-minute reconciliation workload would save 57.45 minutes, or 20.9% of 275.1, rounded down to 20%. The evidence does not establish that instrumentation or scaffolding alone will achieve that reduction.
